overview: This Senate resolution supports the goals of Choose Respect Day, which Congress set for October 1 each year to raise awareness of domestic violence and encourage respect in relationships, especially among teens and young adults. It notes the scale of intimate partner violence in the United States, its effects on children, families and survivors' health, its link to family homelessness, and the dangers police face in responding to domestic violence calls. The resolution encourages individuals, organizations, and all levels of government to mark the day with proclamations, activities and education aimed at changing the culture around tolerating domestic violence. The Senate adopted it by unanimous consent on October 3, 2025.
for: Supporters say formally recognizing the day helps raise awareness of domestic violence and encourages young people to build safe, respectful relationships.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide new funding for domestic violence prevention or survivor services.
